# Mabel Colby

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004)</sub>
- **Rank:** Sophomore (Second Year) at Wexcombe College  <sub>[v3 c9 P8](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0008), [v3 c16 P4](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0004)</sub>
- **Origin:** Vancouver  <sub>[v4 c1 P22](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0022), [v4 c3 P16](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0016)</sub>
- **Role:** Teacher  <sub>[v3 c9 P7](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0007), [v4 c1 P22](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0022)</sub>
- **Titles:** the 'rose-red' girl  <sub>[v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004)</sub>

## Appearance

Mabel is a striking young woman with dark eyes. At Regent's Academy, she was recognized as the preeminent beauty among the Second Year students.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006)_

## Personality

Mabel possesses a heart filled with light, multicolored dreams and imaginations, alongside a creative and contemplative nature. She is given to humor, mockingly quoting poetry to her companions, and tends to fling her manuscript pages across the floor while writing.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v3 c16 P40](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0040), [v3 c36 P21](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0021)_

## Traits

- imaginative and dream-filled  <sub>[v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004)</sub>
- contemplative and creative scholar  <sub>[v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004)</sub>
- fear of returning to boardinghouses  <sub>[v3 c27 P10](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0010)</sub>

## Abilities

- instructing across diverse subjects and nine grade levels  <sub>[v3 c9 P8](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0008)</sub>
- essay writing for academic societies  <sub>[v3 c36 P21](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0021)</sub>
- managing household financial records  <sub>[v3 c17 P1](../source/v03-c17.md#nw-v03-c17-p0001)</sub>

## Goals

- write a realistic paper titled 'The Trials of a Country Schoolmarm'  <sub>[v3 c9 P8](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0008)</sub>
- pursue higher education at college instead of continuing isolated rural teaching  <sub>[v3 c9 P8](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0008)</sub>

## History

While attending Regent's Academy, Mabel befriended Nell Harcourt and Honora Hollis, forming part of a circle of contemplative and driven scholars. After finishing her third year at Regent's, she spent years working as a schoolteacher in an isolated country school, instructing students across nine grades. Tired of the heavy demands and misconceptions surrounding rural teaching, she decided to attend Wexcombe College as a Sophomore. Mabel rented Tabby's Place alongside Nell, Honora, and Cressy Lindsay, with her Aunt Euphemia taking over household duties and Mabel managing the household financial records. During her time at college, she actively participated in literary activities, including reading old Story Club manuscripts and writing essays for the Philomathic Society. After completing her studies, she moved to Vancouver, where she took up work as a schoolteacher.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v3 c9 P7](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0007), [v3 c9 P8](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0008), [v3 c10 P47](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0047), [v3 c10 P52](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0052), [v3 c16 P4](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0004), [v3 c17 P1](../source/v03-c17.md#nw-v03-c17-p0001), [v3 c35 P44](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0044), [v3 c36 P21](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0021), [v4 c1 P22](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0022), [v4 c3 P16](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0016)_

## Quotes

> Why on earth aren’t you coming? The grave is prepared by us. ‘What silent still and silent all?’  <sub>[v3 c16 P40](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0040)</sub>

> I am extremely happy that Tabby’s Place remains ours for one more year. My fear was that they would return, which would shatter our delightful small haven here, casting us unfortunate, inexperienced young ones back into the harsh realm of boardinghouses.  <sub>[v3 c27 P10](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0010)</sub>

> I’m feeling down and disheartened too. Nothing appears to have any value. Even my thoughts are ancient. I’ve already pondered every single one. What purpose does life serve anyway, Nell?  <sub>[v3 c35 P31](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0031)</sub>

> It does—yet I entertain no jealousy. I hold affection for Nell, and Cyril pleases me. Everyone asserts that her marriage will be a splendid one, and at present even Mrs. Lisle finds her delightful. Everything appears as though it were fashioned in paradise, though I harbor my reservations. Take whatever you can from that, Aunt Euphemia.  <sub>[v3 c38 P16](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0016)</sub>
